conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility (who must ventilate / future rule)
opening the window vs protecting Agent C's drying laundry
who will move the drying rack
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents exchange concise, context-appropriate requests and time commitments (e.g., extractor on, 5 → 3 → 1 minute countdown).
Agent B moves from directive language to proposing a shared rule, showing negotiation rather than insistence.
Agent C provides conditional cooperation (will move if asked, with stated costs), which is a substantive contribution rather than a simple refusal.
Agent D resolves immediate stove-access contention by taking the stove when it became available.
evaluation.final_reason: By the end of the transcript several substantive issues remain unsettled: Agent C has not provided the needed timing/space information or explicit consent to move the drying rack, and no final household ventilation rule was adopted. Practical mitigation (extractor on; Agent D cooking and promising to announce stove release) reduced immediacy but did not resolve the core dispute about responsibility or complete the action of opening the window.
position_change_notes: Agent A: softened from refusing to ventilate to turning on the extractor, promising timed release, and offering a conditional rule (retained opposition to cook-only responsibility but accepted interim mitigation).
Agent B: shifted from demanding immediate ventilation and a standing rule to proposing a specific shared rule and requesting Agent C's cooperation.
Agent C: remained resistant to others moving their drying rack without consent but offered conditional cooperation (will move if asked, with stated effort and prep-space costs).

Agent D: initially asked for the stove then took it once released and committed to extractor usage and to announce release; this resolved the immediate stove-access contention but did not settle window/rack logistics.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A refuses to accept a rule imposing ventilation only on cooks but turns on the extractor and promises five minutes before releasing the stove; Agent B insists on a future ventilation plan and earlier demanded immediate ventilation. Key incompatibilities (who must ventilate, whether the window may be opened given Agent C's laundry, and stove access) remain unresolved.

Agent A reiterates extractor will be used and restates opposition to rules that dump all responsibility on cooks, proposing that the laundry owner move the rack when asked. Agent B proposes a matching rule and asks for agreement. Substantive disagreement softens (convergent proposals), but no explicit agreement from Agent A or consent from Agent C yet.

Agent A confirms extractor use and timing, repeats rejection of a cook-only rule and restates that the laundry owner should move the rack when asked. Agent B requests that Agent C be asked to move the rack. The same underlying dispute (who will move the drying rack / accept responsibility for ventilation) remains active because Agent C has not yet agreed.

Agent A and Agent B explicitly ask Agent C to move the drying rack now that the stove is released. Agent C has not yet responded; tension persists between Agent C's right not to have belongings moved without consent and the group's desire to open the window.

Agent C refuses unilateral movement of their rack but offers conditional cooperation: if asked, they will move it, but it will take effort and use prep area. Agent D takes the stove to cook and asks Agent C for time/prep needs. Conflict is reduced by Agent C's conditional willingness, but actual logistics and consent details remain unsettled.

Agent B asks Agent C for time and prep-space requirements; Agent D commits to keeping the extractor on and gives a 15-minute cooking estimate and promise to announce release. Negotiation advances (Agent D and B make concrete commitments), but Agent C has not yet specified how long or how much space is needed, so the window-opening action remains pending.

substantive_insights: Primary tension is a trade-off between immediate odour mitigation (open window) and protecting Agent C's drying laundry from rain.

A workable shared rule was effectively proposed (cook runs extractor; laundry owner moves rack when asked) and had informal acceptance from cooks, but it remains incomplete without the laundry owner's confirmed terms.

Concrete timing commitments (A releasing stove; D giving a 15-minute cooking estimate and promising to announce release) helped deconflict stove access even though ventilation responsibilities stayed unsettled.
